memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And what he did to Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab the Reubenite, when the earth opened its mouth right in the middle of all Israel and swallowed them up with their households, their tents and every living thing that belonged to them. But it was your own eyes that saw all these great things the Lord has done. - Deut 11:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses recalls a sobering event: the judgment on Dathan and Abiram, who led a rebellion against God's appointed leadership and were swallowed up by the earth. It is a hard memory, but Moses includes it deliberately. Israel had witnessed not only God's saving power but also His judgment on rebellion. They had seen with their own eyes that God is not to be trifled with — that stubborn rebellion against Him has real and serious consequences.

We prefer to dwell on God's kindness and quietly skip over His justice, but a true picture of God holds both together. The same God who parted the sea also judged rebellion. This is not a contradiction; it flows from His holy and consistent character. God's justice is not cruelty — it is His unwavering commitment to what is right. And His judgments serve as warnings, meant to turn His people away from the destructive path of rebellion before it consumes them.

For us, these accounts are recorded "as warnings" so that we would not fall into the same rebellion (1 Cor 10:11). They call us to take God seriously and to walk humbly before Him. Yet here is the gospel hope: the judgment that our own rebellion deserves fell on Jesus at the cross. He bore the wrath we had earned so that we could be spared. We do not read of Dathan and Abiram with smug superiority, but with humble gratitude — recognizing that but for God's mercy in Christ, we too would stand condemned. Let God's justice sober you, and let His mercy in Christ move you to worship.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does my picture of God include His justice, not only His kindness?
- How do accounts of God's judgment serve as warnings for me today?
- How does the cross change the way I read passages about judgment?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are both merciful and just, and I take You seriously. Thank You that the judgment my rebellion deserved fell on Jesus at the cross. Keep me humble and grateful, walking in reverence before You, sobered by Your justice and moved by Your mercy. Amen.
